title: chalk-talk ↔ a teacher at the board

learning.goal: Understand the path from a request to a self-contained HTML lesson: outline, recipe, build checks, offline player.
learning.question: Someone asks to make the arrow blue in a lesson already delivered. Which parts of this path run again?
learning.answer: Only the end of it: Claude edits that one step's style in the recipe, then build.mjs checks the contract and reviews the layout again and writes a new HTML. The outline is not renegotiated, because the hook and the mold did not change.
learning.caveat: Simplified: the build report has three outcomes (contract error, layout warning, ok), and some checks run when the page opens rather than at build time. Claude never writes the player itself; it only writes the JSON recipe.

steps.text: how does a chalk talk become one file?
steps.say: A good teacher doesn't start drawing right away. First they make sure what the class needs.

steps.label: explain by drawing
steps.say: You ask to explain something by drawing it.

steps.title: agreed outline
steps.say: Claude asks only what is missing, then agrees a four-part outline — before any stroke.

steps.name: document
steps.label: recipe.json
steps.say: Claude writes a small JSON recipe: steps, chapters, narration. Never the player.
build.mjs checks the recipe contract, then opens the drawing in a headless browser and reviews it.
If something breaks, Claude fixes just that and builds again — at most twice.
Out comes one HTML file with the player inside.
Open it anywhere — e-mail it, project it — and the lesson plays, chapter by chapter.
